title: Construct String with Minimum Cost (Easy)
statement: You begin with an empty string `s` and want it to become exactly `target`. In one operation you choose an index `i` of `words`, append `words[i]` to the end of `s`, and pay `costs[i]`; any index may be chosen as often as you like, and `words` and `costs` have the same length. Return the smallest total cost of a sequence of operations that turns `s` into `target`, or `-1` if no sequence of operations can produce `target`.
constraints: target and every words[i] contain only lowercase English letters
signature: int minimumCost(String target, String[] words, int[] costs)
notes:
## Intuition

Because words are only ever appended, every intermediate `s` is a prefix of `target`. So the whole state of the process is one number: how many letters of `target` are already built. Let `dp[i]` be the cheapest way to build the first `i` letters. From a reachable prefix `i`, any word that matches `target` starting at `i` moves us to `i + word.length` at that word's cost. Trying every sequence of words instead (the brute-force idea) grows exponentially with the target's length.

## Approach

1. Create `dp` of size `n + 1` filled with `Infinity`, and set `dp[0] = 0` (the empty prefix is free).
2. Walk `i` from `0` to `n - 1`. Skip `i` when `dp[i]` is still `Infinity`: that prefix cannot be built.
3. For each word index `j`, if `words[j]` appears in `target` starting at `i`, compute `end = i + words[j].length` and lower `dp[end]` to `dp[i] + costs[j]` when that is cheaper.
4. Every jump goes forward, so `dp[i]` is final before position `i` is processed. Return `dp[n]`, or `-1` if it is `Infinity`.

## Example 1, step by step

`target = "abcdef"`, costs: "abdef" 100, "abc" 1, "d" 1, "def" 10, "ef" 5. At `i = 0` only "abc" matches, so `dp[3] = 1`. Positions 1 and 2 are unreachable and skipped. At `i = 3`, "d" gives `dp[4] = 2` and "def" gives `dp[6] = 11`. At `i = 4`, "ef" gives `dp[6] = min(11, 2 + 5) = 7`. Position 5 is unreachable, so the answer is `dp[6] = 7`.

## Complexity

- Time: O(n · m · L) for `n = target.length`, `m` words and longest word length `L`: each position tests each word, and a test compares up to `L` letters.
- Space: O(n) for `dp`.

## Pitfalls

- Greedily taking the cheapest (or the longest) matching word fails: in `"abcd"` with "abc" (1), "a" (2), "bcd" (2), both rules pick "abc" and leave "d" with no word, while "a" then "bcd" costs 4.
- The same word can appear twice with different costs; the `Math.min` keeps the cheaper one automatically.
- Skip unreachable positions; extending from `Infinity` is harmless here but wastes time.
- Report `-1`, not `Infinity`, when `target` cannot be built.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `n` | length of `target` |
| `dp` | `dp[i]`: cheapest cost to build the first `i` letters (`Infinity` if impossible) |
| `i` | length of the prefix we extend from |
| `j` | index of the word being tried |
| `end` | prefix length reached after appending `words[j]` |

narration.2: n is how many letters the finished string must have.
narration.3: dp[i] will hold the cheapest cost to build the first i letters of target; Infinity means not reachable yet.
narration.4: The empty prefix costs nothing to build.
narration.5: Visit every prefix length from left to right; all jumps go forward, so dp[i] is already final here.
narration.6: Is this prefix impossible to build?
narration.7: Then nothing can be appended to it; move on.
narration.9: Try appending each word to the prefix of length i.
narration.10: The word fits only if target continues with exactly these letters at position i.
narration.11: Appending it would build the first end letters.
narration.12: Keep the cheaper of the known cost for end and the cost through this word.
narration.16: An unreachable full length means target cannot be built, which the problem reports as -1.
